articles.title: Intercard Selected by Family Entertainment Group for Nationwide Topgolf Cashless Rollout
articles.summary: Intercard's cashless technology has been chosen by Family Entertainment Group for a nationwide phased rollout across Topgolf venues following a successful seven-location pilot. The deal signals growing operator confidence in cashless payment infrastructure at scale for competitive socializing venues. FEC operators should take note as this partnership sets a benchmark for technology integration in multi-site entertainment operations.

articles.title: Valo Motion Debuts ValoBoard Mixed-Reality Attraction at IAAPA Expo Europe
articles.summary: Valo Motion has announced ValoBoard, a multiplayer mixed-reality board sport attraction that uses weight-shifting on a tilt board paired with full-body tracking to simulate surfing and skateboarding experiences. It will make its world debut at IAAPA Expo Europe in London. The product is a strong candidate for FECs looking to add active, tech-driven attractions with broad demographic appeal.

articles.title: Competitive Socialization's Long-Term Challenge: Designing for Repeat Visits
articles.summary: Industry leaders from FuzionGamz and Level 99 discuss what it will take for competitive socialization venues to move beyond novelty and build lasting customer loyalty. The conversation centers on shifting from directed guest experiences toward open, exploratory environments that give guests more agency. This is essential reading for FEC operators considering or already operating competitive socializing concepts.

articles.title: Six Flags Launches Flex Pay Installment Option for Season Passes and Qualifying Purchases
articles.summary: Six Flags has introduced Flex Pay by Upgrade, allowing guests to purchase season passes and other products of $49 or more and pay over time in fixed monthly installments. The move lowers the upfront cost barrier for guests and could drive higher conversion rates on seasonal memberships. FEC operators should monitor whether installment-based payment options become an industry-wide expectation.

articles.title: accesso CEO Lee Cowie: AI and Context Are the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: New accesso CEO Lee Cowie argues that generic AI tools are insufficient for the attractions industry and that success depends on deploying AI with deep operational context specific to venue management. He views digital experiences as equally important to physical ones and emphasizes that technology is now fundamental to operator success. FEC operators evaluating AI-powered ticketing and in-park purchasing platforms should pay close attention to this perspective.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: InPark Magazine profiles accesso's new CEO on how AI and data analytics are reshaping ticketing and in-park purchasing for attractions operators. The piece explores how removing friction from the guest journey translates directly into revenue gains. FEC operators using or evaluating accesso's platform will find this a valuable strategic read.

articles.title: Ventola Projects Installs Immersive Bowling with Ball-Responsive Projection in Ecuador
articles.summary: Ventola Projects has completed its first South American installation, delivering an immersive bowling experience at PlayGo Entertainment in Ecuador using ball-responsive projection technology developed with VAvR Alliance partner Evogence. The project demonstrates the growing global appetite for technology-enhanced bowling beyond traditional markets. FEC operators looking to differentiate their bowling offerings should watch Ventola's expanding portfolio.

articles.title: Ventola Projects to Launch Tetrapix EM4 Innovation at IAAPA Expo Europe
articles.summary: Ventola Projects will unveil its latest VAvR innovation, the Tetrapix EM4, at IAAPA Expo Europe in London this September. The company is positioning the new product as a significant advancement in immersive venue technology. FEC operators attending IAAPA Expo Europe should put Ventola's booth on their must-visit list.

articles.title: Intercard's Kiosk-Free Impulse Plus Reader Set to Debut at IAAPA Expo Europe
articles.summary: Intercard will showcase its Impulse Plus cashless reader at IAAPA Expo Europe in London, highlighting its kiosk-free design as a key differentiator for venues seeking simplified cashless infrastructure. The reader's standalone functionality reduces hardware overhead for FEC operators. This is a notable product for arcades and FECs looking to modernize payment systems without heavy installation costs.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands into Competitive Socializing with Skill-Based Game Concepts
articles.summary: Jora Vision is growing its competitive socializing portfolio with new concept development focused on skill-based gameplay experiences. The company's approach emphasizes technology integration that enhances guest engagement rather than overshadowing the social element. FEC operators exploring competitive socializing expansions will find Jora Vision's design philosophy relevant to their planning.

articles.title: Premium Halloween: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Interactive Horror Experiences
articles.summary: Six Flags has partnered with Plague Productions and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences to create The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, a premium interactive horror attraction for the Halloween season. The collaboration reflects a broader industry trend toward higher-priced, immersive seasonal events that command separate admission. FEC operators running haunted attractions or seasonal events can look to this partnership as a model for elevating their Halloween programming.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 111: Frictionless Guest Experience as the Central Theme
articles.summary: InPark's latest issue focuses on technology-driven frictionless guest experiences, covering ticketing, in-park purchasing, and immersive design across attractions. Contributors include accesso, Jora Vision, and Alterface, offering a broad industry perspective on reducing guest friction. FEC operators will find this issue a useful survey of where the industry is heading on the technology and design front.

articles.title: Study Finds Major Handwashing Gaps at Amusement Parks and Attractions
articles.summary: New research from the 2026 Clean Hands Index analyzed 45 handwashing environments at amusement parks and attractions and found that none met all recommended hygiene standards. The findings highlight a potentially overlooked area of guest experience and risk management for venue operators. FEC operators should audit their restroom and handwashing facilities in light of these findings.

articles.title: Fun Spot America Atlanta Assets to Go to Auction on October 14
articles.summary: Following the permanent closure of Fun Spot America's Atlanta park in August 2026, the venue's equipment and assets will be auctioned on October 14. The auction presents an opportunity for FEC operators and suppliers to acquire amusement equipment at potentially favorable prices. The closure and subsequent asset liquidation also serve as a cautionary case study in regional park viability.

articles.title: Six Flags Acquires ArieForce One Coaster from Closed Fun Spot America Atlanta
articles.summary: Six Flags has purchased the ArieForce One steel roller coaster from the shuttered Fun Spot America Atlanta park, with plans to install it at one of its properties during the 2028-2029 season. The coaster, built by Rocky Mountain Construction, had built a strong enthusiast following before the park's closure. The acquisition underscores how major operators can opportunistically expand their ride inventory through distressed park closures.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Opens in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new FEC billing itself as Texas' largest has opened in Houston, marking a significant addition to the market for indoor family entertainment in one of the country's most populous metros. The venue's scale suggests a trend toward large-format, multi-attraction FEC development in major urban markets. Operators and investors tracking competitive FEC openings should note this Houston development.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Posts Summer 2026 Growth but Rising Costs Squeeze Margins
articles.summary: India's amusement and entertainment industry saw meaningful attendance growth during summer 2026, but operators are facing pressure from rising operational costs that are compressing profit margins. The trend reflects a global challenge facing FEC operators balancing post-pandemic demand recovery with inflation-driven cost increases. Suppliers and investors with exposure to emerging markets should monitor how Indian operators navigate this margin squeeze.

articles.title: India's IAAPI Calls for GST Reduction to Fuel Amusement Industry Growth
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries has formally called on the government to rationalize the Goods and Services Tax applied to amusement attractions, arguing current rates suppress consumer demand and hinder industry growth. The lobbying effort highlights how tax policy remains a significant structural challenge for FEC-style businesses in high-growth emerging markets. Operators and investors with international interests should track this regulatory development.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, drawing an outpouring of community sentiment on social media. The closure is a reminder that even established, beloved FEC venues face long-term sustainability challenges. Operators should examine the factors behind closures of this type as market dynamics and consumer preferences continue to shift.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is opening a new location on Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, featuring arcade games and a trampoline park. The opening adds to Launch's expanding footprint of active-entertainment FEC venues. Industry observers tracking the trampoline park and FEC franchise growth market should note this new location.

articles.title: New Indoor FEC Opens in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee Over Labor Day Weekend
articles.summary: A new indoor family entertainment center opened in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee just in time for the Labor Day weekend, reflecting continued suburban FEC development in the Nashville metro area. The timing of the opening around a holiday weekend is a smart strategy for maximizing initial foot traffic and brand awareness. Regional FEC operators tracking market saturation in the Southeast should note Nashville's growing FEC inventory.

articles.title: Massachusetts Amusement Center Adds Four-Story Free-Fall Ride
articles.summary: A Massachusetts amusement center has installed a new four-story free-fall ride, significantly upgrading its thrill attraction offerings. Adding a signature anchor ride is a proven strategy for driving new visitor interest and media coverage. FEC operators considering capital investments in differentiated attractions will find this a relevant example.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Cuts Hollywood Bowl Target Over Summer Heatwave Impact on Indoor Footfall
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank has lowered its price target for Hollywood Bowl after a summer heatwave was found to have reduced indoor entertainment footfall at the UK bowling operator's venues. The analyst note is a rare public acknowledgment of how extreme weather events can materially affect FEC attendance and revenue forecasts. FEC operators and investors should factor climate and weather volatility into demand planning models.

articles.title: Sportainment: How Sports Venues Are Evolving Into Full Entertainment Ecosystems
articles.summary: An analysis of the sportainment trend explores how live sports events are increasingly packaging entertainment, hospitality, and immersive experiences alongside the core sporting event to capture the attention economy. The piece draws parallels to how FECs must think beyond their primary attraction to build holistic entertainment environments. Operators looking to understand the broader competitive landscape for discretionary leisure spending will find this analysis valuable.

articles.title: Dynamic Creatures Launches Interactive Character Robots for Entertainment and Hospitality Venues
articles.summary: Dynamic Creatures has officially launched as Boston Dynamics' official entertainment and hospitality partner, developing mobile character robots capable of navigating guest environments, understanding interaction context, and responding in real time. The company is already working with a major theme park and retailer on character experience deployments. FEC operators interested in next-generation guest interaction technology should monitor this company as it moves from theme parks toward broader entertainment venues.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Interactive Experience Design in Themed Entertainment
articles.summary: Alterface, a specialist in interactive dark ride and shooting attraction technology, is marking its 25th anniversary with a retrospective on its design philosophy and project portfolio. The company's work spans FEC-adjacent interactive experiences across major global attractions. FEC operators designing interactive attractions can draw inspiration from Alterface's long track record of creating engaging, repeatable guest experiences.

articles.title: New LaPorte, Indiana FEC to Feature Bowling, Mini Golf, Arcade, and More
articles.summary: A new indoor family entertainment center is being developed in LaPorte, Indiana, offering a multi-attraction lineup including bowling, mini golf, and arcade games. The project is representative of the continued rollout of blended-attraction FEC formats in mid-size Midwestern markets. Suppliers and developers tracking new FEC construction activity should note this project.

articles.title: InPark Editorial: Letting the Guest Experience Lead Technology Decisions
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's publisher argues that the most effective use of technology in attractions is when it serves the experience rather than becoming the focus itself, using examples from ticketing, in-park purchasing, and immersive design. The editorial frames frictionless guest experience as both a competitive advantage and an operational philosophy. FEC operators grappling with technology investment decisions will find this a useful framing piece.

articles.title: Siam Park's Summer Night Event Drives 20% Attendance Increase
articles.summary: Siam Park reported a 20 percent increase in attendance during its eight-week Siam Night summer event, which transformed the water park into a nighttime festival experience. The results demonstrate the significant revenue and attendance upside of after-hours seasonal programming for attractions operators. FEC operators running evening events or considering extended operating hours should view these results as strong validation of the strategy.

articles.title: Slick City Action Park Targets Fresno Market With Indoor Slide Experience
articles.summary: Slick City Action Park, an indoor slide-based entertainment concept, is entering the Fresno, California market, according to local reporting. The brand represents a newer category of active indoor FEC attraction built around large-format slide systems. FEC operators and investors tracking emerging active-entertainment concepts should follow Slick City's expansion trajectory.
